title: Operator claim sanitizer and jurisdictional KMS arbiter + audit sampling controls
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Enterprise customers asked for tighter runtime controls to prevent accidental leakage of operator-level attributes into audit exports and downstream KMS selection. This PR introduces two related runtime controls: 1) an Operator Claim Sanitizer middleware that removes or pseudonymizes sensitive operator claims before they flow into the audit pipeline or cross-service headers, and 2) a Jurisdictional KMS Arbiter that deterministically selects a KMS endpoint (primary CMK or allowed external provider) based on a combination of tenant residency claims, service-level jurisdiction config, and explicit consent flags. Additionally, we add a configurable Audit Sampling Control to reduce PII surface in high-volume tenants while preserving forensic evidence for compliance. Motivation: reduce regulatory risk (GDPR/Schengen/UK sovereignty), prevent accidental export of identifying operator metadata, and provide a transparent KMS decision path for auditors. Scope: - Auth path change is surgical and runs as an opt-in feature flag for the first rollout cycle. - Arbiter runs during per-request key-provider resolution and emits deterministic decision metadata to the audit stream (hashed when configured). - Audit sampling is configurable per-tenant with retention of sampled trace IDs for retrospective rehydration. Checklist: - [x] Implement claim sanitizer middleware (redwood/services/authorization) - [x] Implement KMS arbiter and policy rules engine (redwood/services/kms-arbiter) - [x] Add unit and integration tests for region pinning and consent flows - [x] Add docs & operational runbook (docs/compliance/kms-arbiter.md) - [x] Add feature flag gating + rollout plan in releases/flags.yaml - [x] Performance microbenchmarks and load test notes included in PR conversation Breaking considerations: sanitizer defaults to a conservative safe-mode that only strips high-risk claims (operator_email, operator_raw_jwt, caller_debug_flags). Customers can extend the claim allowlist through service-config. Rollout plan: 1) Canary on internal staging (2% of traffic) for 48h; 2) Open beta to opt-in customers; 3) Global enable via feature flag after 7-day observation and no regressions. Observability: new metrics redwood.auth.sanitizer.filtered_claims, redwood.kms_arbiter.decisions, redwood.audit.sampling_rate plus traces and decision tags. Audit footprint change: we add a hashed decision_id when sampling is enabled to allow reconstruction while avoiding PII in the main audit record.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in Operator Claim Sanitizer middleware to strip/pseudonymize high-risk operator attributes, and a Jurisdictional KMS Arbiter to deterministically select a KMS provider based on tenant residency and consent. Includes audit sampling controls to reduce PII in high-volume tenants while retaining pointers for forensic rehydration. Feature is behind a feature flag and rolled out via canary.
operational_notes: Runbook: docs/compliance/kms-arbiter.md. Suggested canary knobs: releases.flags.operator_claim_sanitizer=enabled, releases.flags.kms_arbiter=canary(2%). Monitor redwood.auth.sanitizer.filtered_claims and redwood.kms_arbiter.decisions for anomalies. If increased audit drop noticed, revert flag or increase sampling_rate. Compliance/GRC: store mapping of policy_fingerprint -> human-readable rule in secure evidence store (see runbook).
notes_on_perf: Microbench (8vCPU): median auth path +0.5ms, p95 +2.1ms; KMS arbiter adds ~1.4ms on average for policy lookup (in-memory cache hit). End-to-end e2e under 1% latency regression at 95th when running on default staging load. Details in PR conversation.
qa_instructions: 1) Enable feature flags in staging; 2) Create a tenant with residency=eu and consent=false and exercise key resolution flow; 3) Assert audit entry contains hashed policy_meta and decision_id; 4) Toggle audit sampling to 10% and confirm sampled trace ids retained for rehydration; 5) Run regression suite and confirm no auth regressions.
notes: This PR is intended as a compliance-facing change that minimizes behavioral surprise for existing customers by defaulting to conservative sanitization. Feature flags and config expose extensions for customers who require richer operator metadata for debugging.
